candidates.name: Horizontal fruit on the plant
candidates.author: Pollinator
candidates.strengths: One unmistakeable courgette runs across the picture. The surrounding stems and irregular leaves give us a natural arrangement; the small yellow flower is secondary.
candidates.drawing: Keep the long fruit and a few framing leaves. Omit soil, damaged leaf detail and most crossing stalks. Use cream behind the drawing, with one restrained leaf overflow. Preserve the generous gap above the title.

candidates.name: Two overlapping fruits
candidates.author: Thomas Parker / Pexels
candidates.strengths: The two different fruit sizes and crossing angles offer more movement and depth. This is a useful alternative if the single-fruit composition feels too quiet.
candidates.drawing: Keep both fruits and their natural overlap. Omit the large upper blossom and simplify the dense foliage; otherwise it risks repeating the flower-led cover problem. The crop marks the useful fruit area, not a finished photograph strip.
